==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Serilog&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/SerilogTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Serilog&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Serilog;

// Verify.Serilog: Captures the Serilog events written during a test and includes them in the snapshot under log.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Serilog
// Note: Initialize() replaces the process wide Log.Logger with a logger writing to Verify's sink,
// so a test setup that configures Serilog itself is overwritten.
// Note: Anything logged outside a recording throws, so Recording.Start() has to run before the
// code under test logs. Logging during host startup is the usual trap.
// Note: Entries land in the shared recording under log, which is the name every logging extension
// uses, so Recording.IgnoreNames cannot tell them apart.
// Note: VerifySerilog.IgnoreSourceContext<T>() and its string overload, in the module initializer,
// drop events whose SourceContext matches a known type.
// Note: Initialize takes an optional Action<LoggerConfiguration> for destructuring policies,
// enrichers and filters. Using it means calling Initialize explicitly, before InitializePlugins().
// Note: The callback runs after MinimumLevel.Verbose, Enrich.FromLogContext and the sink are wired
// up, so it layers on top of those defaults.
public class SerilogTests
{
    // Everything logged between Recording.Start() and the verification is added to the snapshot
    // under the name log, so the assertion covers what the code logged as well as what it
    // returned. Nothing has to be passed to Verify for the log entries to appear.
    [Fact]
    public Task Logging()
    {
        Recording.Start();

        var result = Method();

        return Verify(result);
    }

    // Message template properties are kept as structured values rather than being flattened into
    // the rendered message, so a changed property is a one line diff.
    [Fact]
    public Task StructuredProperties()
    {
        Recording.Start();

        Log.Information("Hello {Name}, you are {Age}", "World", 42);

        return Verify("result");
    }

    // Recording.Stop() returns the entries instead of adding them, so they can be filtered or
    // combined with other values before being verified.
    [Fact]
    public Task StopRecording()
    {
        Recording.Start();

        Log.Warning("The warning");

        var entries = Recording.Stop();
        return Verify(entries);
    }

    // Stands in for the code under test. It logs through the global Serilog Log, which
    // Verify.Serilog has pointed at its own sink.
    static string Method()
    {
        Log.Error("The Message");
        return "Result";
    }
}
